site.name: nukko — Korean reality cast on Instagram
site.description: An archive of the Instagram accounts of Korean reality show cast members, organised by show and season. Only verified accounts are listed, and people with no account are marked as such — so you never search twice.

i-am-solo.name: I Am SOLO
i-am-solo.about: A Korean dating observation show on SBS Plus and ENA, featuring members of the public rather than celebrities. Cast members go by aliases that repeat every season — Yeongsu, Oksun and so on — and some seasons carry a theme, such as divorcees, never-dated, or people in their forties. This page collects the cast of every season from the first, along with the Instagram accounts that have been verified.

singles-inferno.name: Single's Inferno
singles-inferno.about: A Netflix original dating reality series. Contestants live on a bare “Inferno” island and earn a night on “Paradise” island by pairing up. Unlike I Am SOLO, the cast go by their real names on air. This page collects each season's cast along with the Instagram accounts that have been verified.

takedown.title: Takedown & corrections
takedown.description: Take my account down, the wrong account is linked to me — how to ask, and how fast it is handled.
takedown.intro: {brand} only lists accounts that were made public on the show or set to public by the person themselves. Even so, if you want yours down, we take it down. Photos too. We do not ask why.
requests: Remove or fix my real name, age, or job
An account that has nothing to do with me is linked to my name
The program, the season or the name is wrong
takedown.requestsNote: You can report the last two even if you are not the person involved. One wrongly linked account sends a flood of DMs to someone with no connection to the show, so we are glad to hear about it.
takedown.howBefore: Email the address below. Two lines is enough —
takedown.howWhat: the program, the season and the name
takedown.howMiddle: (e.g. I Am SOLO Season 28 Yeongsuk), and
takedown.mailSubject: [Takedown/Correction] Please include the program, season and name
takedown.verifyBody: We have to stop pranks that ask us to take down someone else's account, so the fastest route is anything showing the account is yours — DM us from that Instagram account, or email from the address attached to it. Even when that is hard to confirm, we take it off the site first and talk afterward.
takedown.timeBody: Once confirmed, we delete it right away. You will hear back within 7 days at the latest. Accounts and photos we have taken down never go back up.
takedown.translationNote: This English text is a translation. Where the two differ, the Korean original governs.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What this site publishes, and what it keeps about visitors.
privacy.cast1: We publish the name used on the show (some programs use aliases), the real name where it is already public, the age and job at the time of airing, and public Instagram accounts. Photos are sometimes included. We keep a separate record of when and how each account was verified, and we use that record when handling a correction request.
privacy.cast2: All of it comes from the broadcast and from public sources — never collected from the person directly. Private accounts and unverified guesses are not published. If you ask us to take something down, photos included, we do it without asking why.
privacy.visitor1: There are no accounts and no logins. No screen on this site asks for your name or contact details.
privacy.visitor2: We use Vercel Web Analytics for traffic stats. Which pages were opened, where visitors came from, and rough device and browser types are counted anonymously. These stats use no cookies and do not identify visitors individually.
privacy.visitor3: If you email us, your address and message stay in that mailbox. We delete them once the request is handled.
privacy.processor: Hosting and traffic stats run on Vercel Inc. (USA). Visiting the site leaves an access record there. Ads are served by Google LLC (USA). Nothing is handed to or sold to anyone else.
privacy.ads: We show ads through Google AdSense. Google and its advertising partners may use cookies to select ads based on your visits to this and other sites. You can turn personalized ads off in Google's ad settings.
privacy.rights: You can ask to see, correct, or delete information about yourself. We do not ask why, and once it is confirmed we delete it right away.
privacy.translationNote: This English text is a translation. Where the two differ, the Korean original governs.

about.title: About
about.description: What this site is, how each account is verified, and what it will not list.
about.intro: {brand} is an archive of the Instagram accounts of Korean reality show cast members, organised by program and season. It exists for the moment right after an episode airs, when you want to know who that person was.
about.why1: Search a cast member's name the day after an episode airs and you get forum threads, blog posts from years ago, and lists that each name a different handle. There is no way to tell which one is right without opening every account, and most people give up before they do.
about.why2: A wrong handle does not only waste the searcher's time. One aggregator listed the account of Yeongsu from I Am SOLO season 30 with an extra underscore at the end of the handle. That account belonged to a Portuguese skincare brand with three followers. Had that list sent people there, the brand would have received direct messages without ever knowing why.
about.why3: So this site checks one line at a time instead of growing the list. It publishes only what has been verified, and says so plainly where nothing was found.
about.what1: Every cast member is in one of three states.
whatStates: Account verified — there is evidence the account belongs to that person. The handle is stored along with the date it was checked and what was checked.
No account — the search was done, and no public account exists. That is a result, not a failure.
Searching — not yet verified. Weak candidates stay here rather than going up.
about.what2: Keeping “No account” as its own state is the clearest thing about this site. Filling an empty slot with a plausible handle makes the list look complete, but the wrong line lands on someone who has nothing to do with the show. A line that says nothing was found saves the next visitor from repeating the same search.
about.how1: A handle goes up only if one of these holds. The higher on the list, the stronger the evidence, and almost every account currently listed came from the first.
howEvidence: The person says so on the account itself — the program and season appear in the display name, bio, or story highlights, or there is a post after the finale introducing themselves by their name on the show.
Two independent sources name the same handle, and opening the account confirms the profile and follower count line up.

Several specific identifying details reported in the press — a real name, the name of a shop or clinic they run, a former career, things unlikely to coincide — match the profile, and the account was opened to confirm it exists and is public. This is the weakest of the three, used rarely; a handful of currently listed accounts rest on it.
about.how2: Either way the Instagram page is opened directly. Being written down in someone's list is never enough on its own — the account has to exist, be public, and have a profile that matches the person.
about.how3: The date of the check and what was checked are recorded with the handle. Accounts change and disappear, so a fact with no date behind it is not evidence.
exclude: Private accounts, including any account whose visibility could not be confirmed because of a login wall.
Accounts that clearly belong to the right season but cannot be tied to a specific cast member.
Accounts that other people pointed at in comments or tags. However plausible it looks, if the person did not say it themselves it is a guess.

Accounts that match a single identifying detail from a news article. There are plenty of people with the same job, the same city, and the same age. Several specific details have to line up before the third standard above is met.
Press coverage alone. Korean outlets do not print handles by convention, and smaller ones repeat forum guesses as fact.
about.excludeNote: Working through a single season, more than half of the candidates reported as “found” are rejected for these reasons. Six handles printed in one news site's “complete season 28 Instagram roundup” matched no real account at all — the list had been invented. Another handle circulating as season 28's Yeongho turned out to belong to the wedding photographer who shot the couple.
about.photo1: Where a photo appears, its only source is the person's own Instagram profile picture. Screen captures from the broadcast are not used — the copyright there belongs to the production company, which makes it a different question from a request by the person themselves. Images are never hotlinked from another server.
about.programs1: The site started with I Am SOLO and added Single's Inferno. What the cast are called on air differs by program — I Am SOLO uses aliases such as Yeongsu and Oksun, while Single's Inferno uses real names. The name used on the show is the large one on screen, with the real name, age, and occupation on the line beneath it as far as they are known.
about.programs2: A new program starts as a season skeleton; the cast list is confirmed first, then the accounts. A season whose cast list has not been confirmed is left as “cast list in progress” rather than guessed at. Season sizes differ, so stamping in a default roster would invent people who were never on the show.
about.update1: A season still on air can barely be filled in at all, because cast members lock their accounts before broadcast. A month or two after the finale the introduction posts start appearing, and that is when a season gets filled.
about.update2: Seasons are revisited rather than swept once. One season sat at 1 of 12 right after its finale and reached 12 of 12 a few months later. A low verification rate is usually a matter of time.
about.fix1: A single wrong handle sends direct messages to someone with no connection to the show. You do not have to be the person concerned to tell us. Requests to take something down are honoured without asking why.
about.translationNote: This English text is a translation. Where the two differ, the Korean original governs.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Why some seasons are empty, what “No account” means, and how to get a wrong account corrected.
faq.intro: Questions that come up often. How the site works is described in more detail on the about page.

items.q: Why does this season have no accounts at all?
items.a: Cast members usually lock their accounts while the season is airing. A month or two after the finale many of them open up again and post an introduction, and that is when the season starts filling in.
It means the search was done and the person has no public account. Someone who has not been searched yet is marked “Searching” instead. The two are kept apart so you never run the same search twice.

items.q: Why are some accounts still missing?
items.a: Because weak candidates do not go up. Copying handles that circulate in forums would fill the numbers, but verified entries and guesses would be mixed together and no line could be trusted.
Send an email and it will be checked and corrected. You do not have to be the person concerned — a wrong handle hurts whoever owns that account most of all.
It comes down, with no questions asked, and the photo comes down with it. Nothing that has been removed goes back up. The removal page explains how to ask.

items.q: Why are people listed as Yeongsu and Oksun instead of their real names?
items.a: On I Am SOLO the cast are called by aliases on air. The large name on screen is the name used on the show; a real name appears on the line below only when it has been made public. On programs that use real names, such as Single's Inferno, that name takes the large slot instead.

items.q: The same name appears in several seasons. How do I find the right one?
items.a: I Am SOLO reuses 21 aliases across more than 400 cast members, so searching “Yeongsu” alone matches one per season. Type the program or season alongside it to narrow down — “season 22 Yeongsu”, or “Single's Inferno season 4”.

items.q: Where do the photos come from?
items.a: Only from the person's own Instagram profile picture. Screen captures from the broadcast are not used, and images are never hotlinked from another server.

items.q: Do you cover anything other than Instagram?
items.a: Only Instagram for now. Instagram is where people actually look right after an episode, and doing one service properly beats rebuilding the verification standard for each new one.

items.q: Can I send in an account I know?
items.a: Yes, by email, and it will be checked. Handles that arrive are not published as they come in — they have to clear the verification standard described on the about page first.

faq.translationNote: This English text is a translation. Where the two differ, the Korean original governs.
